ובתענית דף ך"ה כו' דת"ר היו מתענים (עבור גשמים) וירדו להם גשמים קודם הנץ החמה (דעדין לא חל עליהם התענית) לא ישלימו את התענית לאחר הנץ החמה (שכבר חל עליהם התענית) ישלימו דברי ר"מ רבי יוסי או' קודם תשע שעות לא ישלימו לאחר תשע שעות ישלימו שכן מצינו באחאב שהתענה מט' שעות ולמעל' שנא' הראית כי נכנע אחאב מפני וגו' ופירש"י וז"ל שכן מצינו שאין לך אדם בעולם שאין תענית חל עליו מט' שעות ולמעלה אפי' בני מלכים שדרכן לאכול בט' שעות שעד ג' הן ישנים ושוהין שש שעות ואוכלים וכדאמרי' בפסחים אפי' אגריפס המלך שרגיל לאכול בט' שעות ביום לא יאכל בערב פסח עד שתחשך כו' עכ"ל רש"י וע"כ בני מלכים מתנהגים בזמן סעודת' כת"ח הרי דו' שעות של ת"ח מתחילים משעה שקמים ממטותיהן כדמתחילים לחשבן בבני מלכים אחר ג' שעות לפי שעד אותו זמן הן ישנים א"כ דומי' דהכי ד' שעות לכ"ע היינו ג"כ משעה שקמו ממטותיהן והא מוכח מפסחים דהארבע שעות מחשבי' מע"ה כנ"ל:
ומכאן י"ל כו' ע' סי' רפ"ח. ר"ל דשם מבואר דאין להתענות בשבת אפי' שלא לשם תענית עד חצות דאחר זה הוי כזורק אבן לחמת ותיקשי מנהג העול' אבל לפמ"ש סי' רפ"א בשם הב"ח דבשבת מאחרים לקום ממטותיהן משום תענוג שינה ואותן שש שעות חשבי' משעה שקמים ממטותיהן א"כ א"ש המנהג דאין מאריכים כ"כ יותר משש משעה שקמים ממטותיהן:
machatzit_hashekel.en:
(א) (section 1) "Hour four means," etc., as the Mechaber wrote in siman 483 — meaning that from there are two reasons that we count these hours from alos hashachar, and also that seasonal hours are required; for they said there that by Torah law chametz on erev Pesach is permitted in eating until midday, and Rabbi Yehudah said: by rabbinic law one does not eat chametz except until the end of four hours; and every fifth hour it is forbidden in eating and permitted in benefit; and at the beginning of the sixth hour one must burn it. They said: what is the reason? Lest they err between before midday and after midday — but this is recognizable from the sun's course; and they answered Rava's second answer, that they are concerned for an overcast day when there is no recognition by the sun, and thereby they might err to eat also after midday; and the Gemara challenged: also in the fourth hour let us be concerned they will err — and it should have been proper to forbid also in the fourth hour; and they answered: the fourth hour is a time of a meal for everyone every day — if so, since the habit to eat at that hour, one feels in himself that hour and will not come to err; behold the permission to eat chametz in the entire fourth hour is since then it is mealtime; and if so, the time of eating chametz and the eating of every person are therefore equal; and since we hold for the matter of the morning meal in siman 483 that we count these four hours from alos hashachar and also count seasonal hours — therefore it is for mealtime, therefore we count thus.**** END BLOCK ****

(2) And during the fast, page 25, 20 of the Detar, they fasted (because of rain) and it rained on them before the hot hawk (dedin did not apply to them the fast) they did not complete the fast after the hot hawk (for which the fast was already applied) they completed the words of Ram Rabbi Yossi O before nine hours they did not complete after nine hours they completed because we found in Ahab that he fasted for 9 hours and above Ahab surrendered because of V. 3 and Pirshii and Zal, for we state that you do not have a person in the world who does not fast, applies to him from 3 hours and above, Efi. The sons of kings whose way is to eat for 3 hours, until the third they sleep and sleep for six hours, and they eat, etc., on Passovers, Efi. After all, the 2 hours of siman 18 start from the hour they get up from their beds, as they begin to count in the sons of kings after 3 hours, per the fact that until that time they sleep the same amount of time, so the 4 hours of siman 18 are the 30th hour of the time they get up from their beds, and it is proven that they break the fast by the four hours from the calculations of siman 18 as above:

(3) And from here one may explain, etc. — see siman 288. Meaning that there it is explained that one should not fast on Shabbat even not for the purpose of fasting until midday, for after that it is like throwing a stone into a sling; and the custom of the world is difficult. But per the words of siman 281 in the name of Bach, that on Shabbat they delay rising from their beds because of the pleasure of sleep, and those six hours are counted from the hour they rise from their beds — if so, there is no custom that they extend more than six hours from when they rise from their beds:
